a_revoir.message:
Jennifer Duncan migratory monarch butterflies are considered endangered, having been added to the IUCN Red List as endangered in 2022 due to a population decline of over 90% in the West and over 80% in the East, note PBS News Weekend and the Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation. While not yet officially listed under the US Endangered Species Act, they are recognized as threatened and under consideration for protection
Maybe they aren't as threatened in your area...But Monarch butterfly counts at the Pismo Beach Monarch Butterfly Grove Pismo Beach. California have experienced dramatic declines recently, with counts dropping from over 16,000 in late 2023 to just under 200 in December 2024. The population has seen extreme fluctuations, with high counts of 24,000+ in 2021 and low counts of 199 in 2020, reflecting a wider, severe decline of Western monarchs. 
Recent Monarch Counts (Pismo Beach Grove)
Late 2025/Early 2026 Season: Counts in late 2025 were again low, with only 556 monarchs recorded in late November, and an even lower count of roughly 197-200 by December/January.
2023-2024 Season: The grove counted roughly 16,044 butterflies in 2023 but plunged to only 205 by Jan 3, 2025,
